findings.reason: the week's public-definition budget is 0, so the section must either justify each name as intended API or delete the imports, and the ambiguity changes what gets deleted.
findings.text: §2's rule "an F401 that is a deliberate re-export goes into `__all__`" adds seven new public definitions (`FluxLoops`, `MagneticProbes` at :56,:87… :58; `equilibrium_chart_alt`, `equilibrium_figure_mpl`, `geometry_figure_mpl`, `radial_profile_figure_mpl`, `time_trace_figure_mpl` at :87–:91), none of which is currently in `__all__`, and the section says neither what it retires nor why nothing can be; the choice is also under-specified (dead import vs. intentional API) and inconsistent with the sibling component classes that already sit in `__all__`

findings.reason: the two sections must be explicitly ordered (config deletion before the sweep, §3's gate measured after §2) or merged, and without that the plan's own exit-0 gates are unreachable as sequenced.
findings.text: `.ruff.toml` is the ruff config the tool actually reads (the plan states this in §3), so §2's instruction to place `allowed-confusables` in `pyproject.toml` writes to a file that is inert until §3 deletes `.ruff.toml`; the plan states no order between §2 and §3, and as written neither order satisfies both done-whens (with `.ruff.toml` present, any kept RUF001/002/003 confusable keeps `ruff check` non-zero for §2; with `.ruff.toml` deleted before §2's fixes, §3's own done-when `ruff check` exits 0 fails on the remaining 55)

findings.reason: the plan should either fold `ruff format` into §2 (or its own commit) or declare it explicitly out of scope and widen the gate to `ruff check .` for CI parity; leaving it unstated makes the headline claim false.
findings.text: the plan's goal is "return the suite and the lint gate to green", but the lint job that owns that gate runs `ruff check .` (line 27) and `ruff format --check .` (line 30); the plan's §2/§3 gates run only `ruff check imas_ink tests` and the plan never mentions `ruff format`, so the CI lint job stays red after the plan lands (measured: `ruff format --check .` would reformat 18 files, e.g. imas_ink/three_d/scene.py, imas_ink/three_d/walls.py, tests/unit/three_d/test_scene_cutaway.py)

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — no new module is proposed; the work is edits to existing files under ruff's existing rules, so there is no interface-vs-behaviour surface to judge.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — `.ruff.toml` is the effective ruff-config owner while `pyproject.toml` is not, yet §2 places `allowed-confusables` in `pyproject.toml` and the plan states no order between §2 and §3, so the owning file is never named on the §2 path.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §2 adds up to seven names to `imas_ink/__init__.py`'s `__all__` (public definitions) without naming what it retires or states why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan defines its lint gate as `ruff check imas_ink tests`, but the gate that actually owns "green" in this repo is `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, which also runs `ruff format --check .` (measured: 18 files unformatted), so the plan does not survey the mechanism that decides the claim it makes.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — no wrapper or layer is added; §2 resolves existing findings in place and §3 deletes a duplicate config rather than wrapping it.
